title: Sevenths on the guitar
description: Memorize shells, string-6/5 offsets for 3 and 7, and G7–Cmaj7 voice leading.

cards.front: What three notes make a shell voicing, and why is that enough?
cards.back: Root, third, and seventh. The third and seventh are the guide tones: they tell you major, minor, or dominant.

cards.front: Why is the fifth the most expendable chord tone?
cards.back: It rarely changes the chord’s identity. Guitar often cannot play all four notes comfortably, and often does not need to.

cards.front: Name the three inversions of a seventh chord, and what Cmaj7/E means.
cards.back: First inversion: third lowest. Second: fifth lowest. Third: seventh lowest. Cmaj7/E is Cmaj7 with E in the bass.

cards.front: From a root, how far are b3, 3, b7, and 7? Also give each as a distance below the root’s octave.
cards.back: ♭3: 3 up / 9 below the octave. 3: 4 up / 8 below. ♭7: 10 up / a whole step below the octave. 7: 11 up / a half step below the octave.

cards.front: Root on string 6 at fret r. Where is the octave, the ♭7, and the maj7?
cards.back: Octave: string 4, fret r+2. ♭7: string 4, fret r. Maj7: string 4, fret r+1. Go back two frets from the octave for ♭7, one fret for maj7.

cards.front: Root on string 6 at fret r. Where are the minor third and the major third?
cards.back: Minor third: string 3 at fret r. Major third: string 3 at fret r+1. Open string 3 is 15 semitones above open string 6.

cards.front: Root on string 5 at fret r. Where are ♭7 and maj7?
cards.back: ♭7: string 3 at fret r. Maj7: string 3 at fret r+1. Open string 3 is 10 semitones above open string 5.

cards.front: Root on string 5 at fret r. Where are the minor third and the major third?
cards.back: Minor third: string 2 at fret r+1. Major third: string 2 at fret r+2. Open string 2 is 14 semitones above open string 5.

cards.front: Do those fret offsets work on every string pair?
cards.back: No. Only the pairs stated. Other pairs differ because G to B is a major third and the other adjacent strings are fourths.

cards.front: Why can a closed-position shell slide to any key?
cards.back: No open strings. Move it up one fret and every chord tone rises one half step. The reliable facts are the chord-tone relationships.

cards.front: Am7 and C6 share pitch classes. What decides the name?
cards.back: Context and the bass. If the bass plays A you hear Am7; if it plays C you hear C6. Lowest note of a voicing is not always the root.

cards.front: Give the string-6 shells for Gmaj7, G7, and Gm7 (frets 6 to 1) and their notes.
cards.back: Gmaj7 3x44xx: G, F♯, B. G7 3x34xx: G, F, B. Gm7 3x33xx: G, F, B♭. One fret changes the 7th (string 4) or the 3rd (string 3).

cards.front: Give the string-5 shells for Cmaj7, C7, and Cm7 and their notes.
cards.back: Cmaj7 x3x45x: C, B, E. C7 x3x35x: C, B♭, E. Cm7 x3x34x: C, B♭, E♭.

cards.front: What are Fmaj7 xx3210, Cmaj7 x32000, Cmaj7/E 032000, and Cmaj7/B x22010?
cards.back: Fmaj7 is root position F A C E. Cmaj7 is root position C E G B E. Cmaj7/E has open E (the third) in the bass. Cmaj7/B has B (the seventh) on string 5 fret 2 in the bass, with C on string 2 fret 1 above it.

cards.front: From G7 shell 3x34xx to Cmaj7 shell x3x45x, which note stays, and which voices move?
cards.back: B on string 3 fret 4 stays: third of G7 and seventh of Cmaj7. F (string 4 fret 3) falls to E (string 2 fret 5), the third of Cmaj7. The root moves G to C.

cards.front: Build Bm7 as a string-6 shell. Frets and notes?
cards.back: Root at fret 7: 7x77xx. B (string 6 fret 7), A (string 4 fret 7), D (string 3 fret 7).

cards.front: Build A7 with the root on string 6, fret 5. Frets and notes?
cards.back: 5x56xx: A, G, C♯. ♭7 on string 4 at fret 5; major third on string 3 at fret 6.

cards.front: Strings 4–1 as 2010 are E G C E. Add open A vs C on string 5 fret 3. What are the two chords, and why?
cards.back: Open A underneath is Am7 (x02010). C on string 5 fret 3 is C major (x32010). Same upper notes; the bass note is the root you hear.

cards.front: Write root, third, and seventh of Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, F7, and B♭maj7.
cards.back: Dm7: D F C. G7: G B F. Cmaj7: C E B. F7: F A E♭. B♭maj7: B♭ D A.

cards.front: For a string-6 G shell, which fingers and which mutes?
cards.back: Finger 1 on the root; finger 2 or 3 for the other notes. Fingertips mute strings 5, 2, and 1.

cards.front: Why are shells the working vocabulary of jazz, funk, soul, and blues rhythm guitar?
cards.back: They leave space for bass, keys, and melody, and they make harmonic motion obvious: you can see and hear exactly which voices move.
